entities.name: Loarn mac Eirc
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Loarn mac Eirc stands as a pivotal, albeit semi-legendary, figure in the early history of the Scotti in what would become Scotland, believed to have flourished in the 5th century CE. As a purported son of Erc of Dál Riata, he is traditionally identified as one of the three founding brothers—alongside Fergus Mór and Óengus—whose migration from Antrim in Ulster to Argyll in western Scotland laid the foundational myth for the kingdom of Dál Riata. His significance transcends mere royal lineage, primarily due to his enduring legacy as the eponymous ancestor of Cenél Loairn, one of the three great kindreds of Dál Riata, whose territorial influence and political power shaped the nascent Scottish realm for centuries and whose name persists in the modern Scottish district of Lorne.

While specific historical events attributable directly to Loarn mac Eirc are scarce and heavily embellished by later genealogical traditions, he is understood to have been instrumental in the initial westward expansion of the Scotti into Argyll. The traditional narrative posits his arrival during a period of significant demographic and political flux, following the decline of Roman authority in Britain and preceding the rise of Anglo-Saxon kingdoms. Loarn's role, as inferred from later chronicles like the *Senchus fer n-Alban*, was likely focused on establishing a sphere of influence in the northern territories of Dál Riata, distinct from the holdings of his brothers. This division of power among the Erc's sons formed the structural basis for Dál Riata's internal political geography.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Loarn mac Eirc, despite his semi-legendary status, is a foundational figure whose purported lineage directly shaped the political and geographical landscape of Dál Riata and subsequently early Scotland. His name endures in the region of Lorne, marking a tangible legacy of early Gaelic expansion.
